mission.display_title: Extend linear models into GLM structure
mission.mission_purpose: Today's Mission exists to extend yesterday's linear-model fluency into GLM structure so you can choose a response family and link with intent — not by software habit.
mission.learning_objective: Explain how a GLM joins an exponential-family response, a linear predictor, and a link for a non-Normal outcome.
mission.concept_focus: Exponential family → linear predictor → link (GLM structure chain).
mission.prior_bridge: Yesterday you finished classical linear models (4.1) — response, explanatory variables, and the linear predictor in the Normal world. Today that same linear machinery expands to responses that are not Normal.
mission.why_now: 4.1 is complete enough to extend; 4.2 is the next lawful Learning Mode node; examiners frequently ask you to choose and justify a link for a non-Normal response — structure first, software second.
mission.expected_benefit: A usable mental map of GLM structure and one justified link choice you can defend — Study Progress evidence for today's Session, not mastery of all of 4.2.
mission.explainability: Assigned because you finished classical linear models (4.1); the exam skill gap now is extending the linear predictor to exponential-family responses via a link — not re-reading least squares.

knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: GLM structure chain
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. In your own words, explain how a generalised linear model joins (1) an exponential-family response, (2) a linear predictor, and (3) a link function. One short paragraph is enough.
knowledge_checks.body: CMP closed. Name all three parts in a coherent order and distinguish the linear predictor from the link.
hints: Start from the response family, then η = Xβ, then g(μ) = η.
Say explicitly that non-Normal responses are in scope.
knowledge_checks.explanation: A GLM joins an exponential-family response, a linear predictor η = Xβ, and a link g(μ) = η. The link is not the same object as the linear predictor; Normal + identity is the special case, not the definition.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: A GLM specifies an exponential-family response, forms a linear predictor η = Xβ, and connects the mean to η through a link function g(μ) = η — so non-Normal outcomes stay inside a linear modelling frame.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Treating GLM as 'linear regression with software' or conflating the link with the linear predictor.
success_criteria: All three parts named in a coherent order.
Linear predictor distinguished from the link.
At least one phrase showing non-Normal responses are in scope.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: canonical link
knowledge_checks.prompt: Name one non-Normal response family used in GLMs (e.g. Poisson or binomial). State its canonical link (or a clearly justified link). In one sentence, why is that link a sensible default for that family?
knowledge_checks.body: Justify from support / mean range — not from software defaults.
hints: Poisson → log; binomial → logit are the usual canonical pairings.
Mention that the link maps the mean into an unrestricted linear predictor.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Canonical links (e.g. Poisson–log, binomial–logit) map the mean into an unrestricted linear predictor while respecting the response support — that is distributional justification, not a software habit.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Poisson with log link (canonical): the mean must stay positive, and log maps (0, ∞) onto the real line for η.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Saying 'because R / glm() defaults to it' without mean-range reasoning.
success_criteria: Link named correctly for that family (canonical preferred).
